title: Re-read prior report and Pi RPC/SDK/session docs with mobile semantic UI lens
Inspect Pi RPC source/types/examples for command/event/UI protocol details

content: Starting a fresh read-through of the previous report and Pi docs with the new assumption that a semantic mobile RPC UI is acceptable.

observation: The existing report was written for the earlier full-TUI-fidelity priority: it recommends PTY/tmux as MVP, while explicitly noting that RPC/SDK is easier for native mobile UX if arbitrary TUI extension compatibility is not required. The new plan should revise that recommendation rather than contradict the prior constraints.

RPC mode is a JSONL stdin/stdout protocol with strict LF framing and explicit command/response correlation. It supports mobile-relevant controls: prompt, steer, follow_up, abort, new/switch/fork/clone sessions, model/thinking changes, queue modes, compaction, retry, bash, stats, messages, commands, session naming, and export.

RPC streams semantic events for rendering: agent/turn/message lifecycle, assistant text/thinking/tool-call deltas, tool execution start/update/end, queue updates, compaction, auto-retry, and extension_error. Tool execution updates carry accumulated partial output, which lets a mobile reducer replace rather than patch tool output.

RPC extension UI is useful but bounded: dialog methods select/confirm/input/editor round-trip through extension_ui_request/response; fire-and-forget notify/status/widget/title/editor-text can be displayed by the client; TUI-specific custom rendering, custom editor/footer/header, working indicators, tool expansion, theme APIs, getEditorText, and custom() are no-op/default/degraded.

For an in-process host bridge, AgentSessionRuntime is the right abstraction for replacing the active session via new/switch/fork/clone/import. After replacement, all session-local subscriptions and extension bindings must be rebound to runtime.session.

Persisted sessions are JSONL v3 trees under ~/.pi/agent/sessions, with session headers, message/model/thinking/compaction/branch-summary/custom/session-info entries. SessionManager.list/listAll/open and tree APIs can power host-side historical session lists and transcript hydration.

Extensions expose powerful TUI-only surfaces (custom TUI components, custom renderers, editor/footer/header/working indicator/theme/autocomplete hooks), but the documented mode behavior says RPC delegates UI to the host JSON protocol while JSON/print are no-op. A mobile RPC plan must define this as a compatibility boundary, not a bug.

The example shows how a custom UI can map RPC events and extension UI requests into a simple interface, but it uses readline for stdout; production clients should instead follow rpc.md/jsonl.js strict LF framing guidance.

content: Re-read the prior report and the Pi RPC/SDK/session/extension docs with the mobile-native assumption. The important shift is that RPC is the simpler direct path only when the compatibility promise is semantic control/rendering, not preservation of arbitrary TUI extension APIs.
Starting source inspection of Pi RPC mode, typed client, JSONL framing, and request/event handling to ground the mobile protocol plan in actual implementation details.

observation: The actual RpcCommand/RpcResponse union matches the docs and is intentionally limited to typed session controls plus extension_ui_response. There is no generic arbitrary TUI frame or custom component channel in the public RPC type surface.

runRpcMode binds extensions with an RPC UI context and subscribes to AgentSession events, outputting every event as JSONL. After runtimeHost new/switch/fork/clone it explicitly calls rebindSession(), reinforcing that a host bridge must treat session replacement as a new subscription/binding lifecycle.

The prompt command is asynchronous: runRpcMode returns no direct handler response; it emits success only through prompt preflightResult once accepted/queued/handled, while later failures arrive as normal events. A mobile bridge should model submitted prompts as accepted versus completed separately.

RPC extension UI dialog requests live in an in-process pending map until response, timeout, abort, or process end. If the mobile transport disconnects during a prompt, the host bridge must either keep the pi process and pending request alive or surface that the mobile app needs to reconnect and respond before timeout.
The implementation serializes via JSON.stringify(value)+'\n' and attaches a custom LF-only reader using StringDecoder; production host/client code should reuse or mirror this, not Node readline.

RpcClient routes records with type=response and matching id to pending requests, and forwards every other record to event listeners. Extension UI requests therefore appear as events that higher-level UI code must render and answer manually.

InteractiveMode constructs `new TUI(new ProcessTerminal(), ...)` in its constructor. This keeps full-TUI remote mirroring harder than RPC mobile UI unless Pi upstream adds terminal/TUI injection points.

content: Inspected RPC types, mode implementation, typed client, JSONL framing, and InteractiveMode constructor. The source confirms the recommended mobile bridge can be a semantic event reducer/command proxy over RPC, with a clearly documented boundary for non-RPC TUI APIs.

Starting re-review of semantic/mobile adjacent implementations, focusing on host daemon/session management, RPC or SDK bridging, mobile-friendly event protocols, pairing/reconnect, notifications, and extension UI handling.

observation: @agegr/pi-web is a semantic browser UI over Pi sessions: session browser grouped by cwd, SSE streaming, fork/tree navigation, branch navigator, model/tool controls, compaction, steer/follow-up, file viewer, and direct reading of ~/.pi/agent/sessions. It validates that a mobile-native Pi UI can be useful without TUI preservation.

woxQAQ/pi-web mirrors Pi RPC types into a browser WebSocket protocol, then extends them with mobile/web necessities: workspace registration/listing, paged session lists, transcript snapshots/upserts/deltas, tree entries, file reads, git branch actions, and queued-message editing. This is a strong shape reference for the Pi-mobile bridge protocol.

woxQAQ/pi-web projects raw Pi message lifecycle events into transcript_snapshot/start/upsert/delta events, batches small deltas (200ms or 32 chars/punctuation/newline), and sends final snapshots after agent_end/compaction. This suggests the mobile client should maintain a local event store/reducer rather than display raw RPC lines directly.

woxQAQ/pi-web's headless UI context returns no-op/defaults for unsupported TUI APIs, while its ExtensionUIBridge forwards select/confirm/input/editor/notify/status/widget/title/editor-text over WebSocket and cancels pending requests on client disconnect. This matches Pi RPC's extension UI boundary.

Detached sessions use createAgentSessionFromServices with cwd-specific built-in tool definitions instead of a long-lived CLI subprocess. In-process SDK can be cleaner for a host daemon, but spawning `pi --mode rpc` is more isolated and language-neutral for a first mobile plan.

BlackBelt dashboard demonstrates a production-grade remote Pi dashboard: bridge extension, server, responsive client, event buffering, session discovery from disk, command routing, prompt/dialog bus, unread/attention state, mobile gestures, and extension-declared GUI modules. Its PromptBus/custom GUI ideas are suitable for a later Pi-mobile extension GUI layer.

BlackBelt dashboard uses `--mode rpc` for headless spawned sessions and keeps separate tmux/terminal paths for interactive sessions. Its RPC keeper/pipe comments highlight an RPC-specific operational issue: pi shuts down on stdin EOF, so long-lived headless sessions need a keeper process or equivalent stdin owner if they must survive bridge restarts.

Codex app-server is a strong semantic-client protocol reference: JSON-RPC with initialize handshake, thread start/resume/fork/list/read, turn start/steer/interrupt, item lifecycle/deltas, approvals as server-initiated requests, file/process APIs, pagination, notification opt-out, and explicit backpressure behavior.

Remodex shows the local-first mobile bridge pattern: trusted device pairing, relay reconnect, spawned local app-server kept warm, bridge-owned handlers for git/workspace/account/notifications, sanitization of large history payloads, push notifications, and app-side reconnect without restarting the local runtime.

Remodex's secure transport provides a concrete E2EE pairing/reconnect model: QR bootstrap, trusted reconnect, X25519 handshake, signed transcripts, encrypted envelopes, outbound sequence numbers, and bounded replay buffer for catch-up after reconnect.

Happy separates durable encrypted updates from ephemeral presence, uses one Socket.IO endpoint with user/session/machine scopes, and layers point-to-point RPC registration/call/ack on the same transport. This maps well to Pi-mobile configured hosts: user/mobile socket, host daemon socket, session sockets, plus RPC calls for spawn/resume/control.

Happy's flat session event protocol (text/service/tool-call-start/end/file/turn-start/end/start/stop) is intentionally small and mobile-renderable. Pi-mobile can either normalize Pi RPC events into a similar app-level event model or store raw Pi events plus derived timeline rows.

Happy's daemon validates version/lock, registers a machine, persists tracked sessions/encryption data, handles remote spawn requests, optionally uses tmux, and rehydrates finished sessions after daemon restart. These are directly applicable to Pi-mobile host daemon design.

pi-acp is a Pi RPC adapter that translates events to another semantic client protocol and preserves Pi session files via a side mapping. It also shows pitfalls: it uses Node readline for Pi RPC stdout, which conflicts with Pi's strict LF-only JSONL guidance, and it omits Pi extension slash commands in ACP.

content: Re-reviewed semantic Pi web adapters and adjacent mobile agent systems. The common successful pattern is a host daemon/bridge that keeps the local runtime authoritative, exposes semantic session/workspace/git/file controls, persists enough event state for reconnect, and treats custom TUI APIs as out of scope or a later GUI extension layer.

Starting architecture synthesis. The plan will answer the user's direct comparison question first, then recommend a Pi RPC subprocess host bridge with semantic mobile protocol and a phased roadmap that keeps full-TUI compatibility as an explicit non-goal for MVP.

observation: Under the user's revised priority, RPC/mobile-native is easier than PTY/tmux because Pi already exposes semantic commands/events and bounded extension UI requests. PTY/tmux is still easier only for exact terminal/TUI extension fidelity.

Recommended MVP boundary: do not stream raw Pi RPC directly to the phone. Build a host daemon that owns the Pi RPC subprocess, strict JSONL parsing, event persistence/replay, session discovery, and workspace/Git helpers; expose a mobile-oriented WebSocket/HTTP API above it.

For the first implementation, spawn `pi --mode rpc` per active session rather than embedding the SDK. It preserves CLI behavior and process isolation, uses Pi's documented protocol, and avoids re-implementing AgentSessionRuntime/rebinding details in the daemon. SDK can become a later optimization.

The mobile app should render a derived transcript/timeline from Pi events, not raw terminal output: user/assistant messages, thinking sections, tool cards with accumulated output, queue chips, compaction/retry notices, extension dialogs, and session state. Store raw events for debugging and re-projection.

Known operational sharp edge: an RPC Pi process exits when stdin closes. The host daemon must remain alive while sessions run; durable daemon restart survival requires a keeper/sidecar or equivalent stdin owner and should be treated as a hardening phase unless restart survival is a launch requirement.

The app-level protocol should include host/machine presence, workspace/session listing, start/open/resume/fork/clone, command forwarding, event replay by monotonic sequence, extension UI response, file/diff/git helpers, and notification attention states. Pi's raw RPC commands are a subsystem, not the whole mobile protocol.

Extension compatibility statement for the plan: support RPC extension UI (select/confirm/input/editor/notify/status/widget/title/editor-text) in the mobile app; unsupported TUI APIs (`custom`, custom renderers, footer/header/editor/working/theme/autocomplete/tool expansion) are out of scope for MVP and can be addressed later with a schema-based GUI extension layer or a PTY fallback tab.

content: Finished the architecture synthesis: RPC-first is the direct path for a native mobile UI; the concrete plan is a configured-host daemon that owns Pi RPC subprocesses, normalizes events into a mobile protocol, persists/replays session state, and adds relay/E2EE/push plus richer workspace/Git features in later phases.
